title: Who May Dwell on Your Holy Mountain?
summary: The psalm asks who may live in the LORD's tent and dwell on his holy mountain. The answer is a portrait of a person of integrity: truthful in heart, harmless to neighbors, loyal to those who fear God, faithful to oaths even when costly, honest with money, and incorruptible in court. Such a person will never be shaken.

from.text: Many scholars classify Psalm 15 as an entrance liturgy

line: Asks who may dwell on God's holy mountain, and answers with a portrait of a trustworthy life: true speech, promises kept when they cost, honest money.
guide: Read the list slowly and ask which line is hardest for you. The psalm does not ask you to be impressive; it asks you to be trustworthy. Pray it as a request to be made that kind of guest in God's house.

stanzas.title: Heading and the question: who may dwell with the LORD?
Integrity in heart, word, and relationships
Honest money, incorruptible justice, and an unshaken life

verses.t: A Psalm of David. O LORD, who may abide in Your tent? Who may dwell on Your holy mountain?
He who walks with integrity and practices righteousness, who speaks the truth from his heart,
who has no slander on his tongue, who does no harm to his neighbor, who casts no scorn on his friend,
who despises the vile but honors those who fear the LORD, who does not revise a costly oath,
who lends his money without interest and refuses a bribe against the innocent. He who does these things will never be shaken.
